context.oneLineDescription: A small self-powered sensor node that harvests ambient energy to run a sensor payload and a low-power telemetry link.
context.highestFidelityTest: Harvester alpha prototype run in an environmental test chamber

DOD-T1-L1.note: Published review of ambient energy harvesting for low-power sensors.

DOD-T1-L2.note: Concept note and sizing model exist.

DOD-T1-L3.note: Bench proof of concept with representative inputs.

DOD-T1-L4.note: Alpha prototype validated in the laboratory.

DOD-T1-L5.note: Chamber testing covered temperature cycling only; vibration and humidity were not exercised.

ctes.name: Energy harvester
ctes.description: The ambient-to-electrical conversion element, including the transducer and its mounting.
ctes.whyCritical: The node's entire power budget depends on it, and no off-the-shelf equivalent meets the size limit.

ctes.name: Power management module
ctes.description: Rectification, maximum-power-point tracking, storage and the load switch.
ctes.whyCritical: It must cope with the harvester's irregular output across the operating temperature range; a failure here stops the payload.

ctes.name: Telemetry firmware
ctes.description: Scheduling, buffering and transmission of sensor records over a low-power radio link.
ctes.whyCritical: Data that is not transmitted is lost; the scheduling logic is new work, not a reused library.

assessments.note: Temperature cycling passed; the vibration profile has not been applied yet.
Environmental chamber time is booked for next quarter.
Laboratory validation is in progress; the only linked item is a facility description, which was rejected as test evidence.
The converter and storage are not yet integrated with the load switch.

assessments.justification: The scheduling concept was sized directly from logged sensor records, so no analytic study on synthetic data was carried out or needed at this level.

assessments.note: Modules run stand-alone but are not integrated.
